summary: A description of a proposed modular graphics and text display with a plasma panel and a small processor. It could work as an intelligent terminal, as a passive terminal imitating other displays, or as an offline minicomputer.

plainLanguage.summary: The DS-1 is a proposed terminal with a screen that remembers which dots are lit and a small computer that controls it. It could work with a network host, translate display data, or run by itself.

subtitle: A proposed terminal with a memory display and its own processor

tldr.problem: The proposal describes a terminal that can handle display work locally as well as communicate with a host.
tldr.mechanism: The DS-1 combines a plasma display whose points retain their state, a minicomputer, a keyboard and communication interfaces.
tldr.outcome: The document proposes three uses: an intelligent network terminal, a translator for other display formats, and an offline system.

today: RFC 296 is a proposal for a modular display terminal. The document describes its planned components and modes of operation.

sections.title: The Three Ways to Use the DS-1
sections.content: The DS-1 proposal brings together a display module, a processor module and a keyboard. In intelligent-terminal mode, its processor handles data from a host or the network. It can also translate existing display commands for its screen, or work offline for local tasks.
sections.plainLanguage: The DS-1 can show network data, adapt display instructions for its own screen, or work without a network connection. A built-in processor handles these jobs.

sections.title: A Display That Keeps Its Image
sections.content:
The display is a plasma panel made of addressable points, or cells. A cell can be turned on or off and retains that state until another signal changes it. This lets the processor change selected parts of the image without refreshing the whole screen or keeping a separate display buffer.

The panel is transparent, so the proposal also describes projecting material such as slides or maps behind it while showing computer-generated graphics.
sections.plainLanguage: Each screen point stays lit or dark until the processor changes it. The processor can update only the parts that need to change.

sections.title: The Processor and Its Connections
sections.content:
The processor stores programs and data, reads keyboard or modem input, and sends coordinates and commands to the display. Its software is intended to handle text editing, character and vector drawing, data management and communication tasks. The proposal also describes a modem and an optional cassette recorder for loading programs.

Local processing lets the terminal reshape incoming data for its display while preserving a character stream compatible with the host.
sections.plainLanguage: The small computer reads what arrives from the keyboard or network, then decides what to draw. Its programs also handle editing and communication with the host.
